catalog.featured-objects.beta-pictoris.d: Webb infrared imagery reveals a main debris disk, a secondary disk tilted about 5 degrees and a curved extension of dust known as the cat’s tail.
catalog.featured-objects.vela-pulsar.des: A neutron star that spins once every 0.089 seconds. The 3D bow-shaped pulsar wind and wandering jet are based on Chandra’s X-ray time series.
catalog.featured-objects.cygnus-x-1.name: Cygnus X-1
catalog.featured-objects.cygnus-x-1.desc: A blue supergiant, HDE 226868, and a stellar-mass black hole orbit each other about every 5.6 days. The stellar wind, accretion disk and jets are illustrated from observations, with display scales adjusted for visibility.
catalog.featured-objects.ngc-6302.name: Butterfly Nebula
catalog.featured-objects.ngc-6302.descri: A planetary nebula whose two gas lobes resemble butterfly wings on either side of a dark dust lane. The 3D model draws on the bright edges and gas filaments visible in Hubble imagery.
catalog.observable-universe.stephans-qui: The foreground galaxy NGC 7320, about 40 million light-years away, shares the view with four galaxies about 290 million light-years away. Galaxy interactions have produced a gas shock and tidal tails.
details.chandraObservationVolume: Chandra X-ray images inform the colors and brightness. Depth and jet motion are illustrated from observed features.
details.quintetModel: Webb imagery informs the color and structure. The foreground separation is compressed to fit the scene, and depths among the background galaxies are illustrative.
canvas.milkyWayBlackHole: 3D view of the Milky Way and its central black hole
canvas.solarNeighborhood: 3D distance map of the solar neighborhood
canvas.unavailable: The 3D viewer could not start in this browser.
catalog.enceladus.surfaceNote: The surface uses the Cassini color mosaic, with illustrative ice jets along the four south-polar fractures.
catalog.titan.surfaceNote: The surface view displays the Cassini infrared mosaic beneath the haze. The grayscale shows surface brightness at a near-infrared wavelength.
catalog.ceres.name: Ceres
catalog.ceres.note: A dwarf planet in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. Its surface uses an observation mosaic from the Dawn spacecraft.
catalog.51-pegasi.51-pegasi-a.name: 51 Pegasi star
catalog.51-pegasi.51-pegasi-a.note: Luminosity is estimated from radius and effective temperature.
catalog.51-pegasi.51-pegasi-b.note: Mass estimate from Cont et al. as listed in the NASA archive. Atmospheric features, display size, and initial position are illustrative.
catalog.51-pegasi.51-pegasi.name: 51 Pegasi
catalog.51-pegasi.51-pegasi.summary: A Sun-like star about 50.4 light-years away. Its hot Jupiter, 51 Peg b, orbits in about 4.23 days.
About 4.37 light-years from the Solar System. It orbits the common barycenter with B in about 79.8 years.
About 4.37 light-years from the Solar System. Its separation from A varies from about 11.2 to 35.4 AU.
catalog.alpha-centauri.alpha-centauri.so: Banik & Kroupa · Galactic orbit model of Alpha Centauri
catalog.alpha-centauri.alpha-centauri.su: The nearest star system to the Sun. The A–B pair is about 4.37 light-years away, and Proxima is about 4.24 light-years away.
catalog.alpha-centauri.binary-orbit.sour: Akeson et al. · A–B binary orbit
catalog.alpha-centauri.planet-note.text: Minimum mass from radial velocities. The circular orbit, plane, and initial phase are simplified, and the display size and surface are illustrative.
catalog.alpha-centauri.proxima-b.name: Proxima b
About 4.24 light-years from the Sun, with an estimated orbital period of 550,000 years around the A–B barycenter. The flare locations and timing are illustrative, based on observed flare activity.
catalog.alpha-centauri.proxima-d.name: Proxima d
catalog.alpha-centauri.spectra.source.ke: Kervella et al. · Spectral types and stellar parameters
catalog.andromeda-satellites.m110.name: Messier 110
catalog.andromeda-satellites.m110.summar: A dwarf elliptical satellite of Andromeda, about 2.69 million light-years away. The model shows its elongated stellar distribution.
catalog.andromeda-satellites.m110.title: Messier 110 · M110
catalog.andromeda-satellites.m32.name: Messier 32
catalog.andromeda-satellites.m32.summary: A compact elliptical satellite of Andromeda, about 2.5 million light-years away. The model shows a bright center and smoothly declining stellar density.
catalog.andromeda-satellites.m32.title: Messier 32 · M32
catalog.andromeda.andromeda.name: Andromeda Galaxy
catalog.andromeda.andromeda.summary: A spiral galaxy about 2.5 million light-years away. The model shows its bright center and disk with stars and dust lanes.
catalog.andromeda.andromeda.title: Andromeda Galaxy · M31
catalog.barnard-star.barnard-star.name: Barnard's Star System
catalog.barnard-star.barnard-star.source: Sperauskas et al. · Galactic orbit model of Barnard's Star
catalog.barnard-star.barnard-star.summar: Four exoplanets orbit this red dwarf, about 5.96 light-years away, with periods of 2.34–6.74 days.
catalog.barnard-star.barnard.name: Barnard's Star
catalog.barnard-star.barnard.note: A red dwarf about 5.96 light-years from the Sun with four confirmed planets. Stellar activity indicates a rotation period of about 140 days. The photospheric patterns are illustrative.
catalog.barnard-star.planets.name: Barnard {0}
catalog.barnard-star.planets.note: Minimum mass from radial velocities. The orbital plane and initial position are simplified, and the surface and size are illustrative.
catalog.epsilon-eridani.epsilon-eridani-: Orbital and mass estimates follow Thompson et al. (2025). The displayed orientation, initial position, size, and atmosphere are illustrative.
A K-type star about 10.5 light-years away. Its Jupiter-mass planet, ε Eridani b, completes an orbit in about 7.34 years.
catalog.featured-objects.betelgeuse.desc: The distance and radius follow the stellar pulsation model estimates of Joyce et al. The surface is illustrative.
catalog.featured-objects.betelgeuse.name: Betelgeuse
catalog.featured-objects.crab-nebula.des: The remnant of a supernova recorded in 1054. The wisps expanding around the central Crab Pulsar are animated using colors based on Webb observations.
catalog.featured-objects.l1527-irs.name: Protostar L1527 IRS
catalog.featured-objects.apep.name: Apep
catalog.featured-objects.apep.descriptio: Colliding winds from two Wolf–Rayet stars form carbon dust. Webb’s mid-infrared image revealed four coiled dust shells, with gaps influenced by a third star. The shell motion and stellar separations are illustrated so they are easy to see.
catalog.featured-objects.hh-30.name: Herbig–Haro 30
catalog.featured-objects.hh-30.descripti: An edge-on protoplanetary disk surrounds a young star in Taurus. The dense dust lane hides the star. Webb observations inform the narrow jet perpendicular to the disk and the wider disk wind around it.
catalog.observable-universe.cartwheel-ga: A collisional ring galaxy in Sculptor. A galaxy collision formed its bright inner ring and its outer star-forming ring. Spokes of gas and dust connect the rings.
catalog.featured-objects.l1527-irs.descr: A young star growing inside a dusty cloud in Taurus. Its outflow has carved hourglass-shaped cavities on both sides of the thin accretion disk. Dust along the line of sight helps account for the orange and blue lobes in Webb’s infrared image.
catalog.featured-objects.hh-211.name: Herbig–Haro 211
catalog.featured-objects.hh-211.descript: A young star in Perseus drives jets in opposite directions. The jets form bow shocks as they strike surrounding gas. The animated knots illustrate the flow traced by Webb’s observations.
catalog.featured-objects.cassiopeia-a.de: A supernova remnant in Cassiopeia. Its outer shell contains dust heated by collisions with surrounding material. Irregular knots and filaments inside the shell come from the exploded star. The model accelerates the expansion to make it visible.
catalog.featured-objects.ngc-3132.name: Southern Ring Nebula
catalog.featured-objects.ngc-3132.descri: A planetary nebula in Vela. A white dwarf that shed its outer layers and a brighter companion sit at its center. The layered gas looks like a ring face-on and like two bowls opening in opposite directions edge-on. The model makes the separation of the central pair easier to see.
catalog.featured-objects.crab-pulsar.des: Webb’s infrared image shows the Crab Pulsar as a bright white point. The surrounding ripples glow with synchrotron radiation from particles released by the pulsar. The model uses colors and brightness patterns from the Webb image to visualize the wisps moving outward.
catalog.featured-objects.crab-pulsar.sou: Crab Pulsar emission model · Assumed radius
NASA Webb · Crab Nebula infrared image
catalog.featured-objects.m13.description: The globular-cluster model shows how the stellar density increases toward its center.
catalog.featured-objects.m13.name: Hercules Globular Cluster
catalog.featured-objects.m45.description: An open cluster in Taurus, shown as a loose collection of bright stars and blue reflection nebulosity.
catalog.featured-objects.m45.name: Pleiades
catalog.featured-objects.eta-carinae.nam: Eta Carinae and the Homunculus Nebula
catalog.featured-objects.eta-carinae.des: A bipolar nebula formed from gas and dust expelled by Eta Carinae during its nineteenth-century Great Eruption. Hubble imagery supplies the colors, and an illustrative 3D model supplies the depth and surface relief.
catalog.featured-objects.v838-monoceroti: Light from the 2002 outburst reached successive layers of dust and produced a light echo. The model loops this illumination sequence using colors based on Hubble imagery.
catalog.featured-objects.ngc-6543.name: Cat’s Eye Nebula
catalog.featured-objects.ngc-6543.descri: A planetary nebula in Draco. Its bright inner shells, overlapping lobes, and faint outer rings are modeled in 3D with colors and structures based on Hubble imagery.
catalog.featured-objects.m57.description: A planetary nebula made of gas expelled by a star. The model shows the bright ring and faint outer gas.
catalog.featured-objects.m57.name: Ring Nebula
catalog.featured-objects.m87-star.descri: The disk incorporates the asymmetric brightness of the ring released by the EHT in 2019. Relativistic Doppler boosting brightens the approaching jet, and the fainter counterjet has also been observed. The motion illustrates features inferred from observations.
catalog.featured-objects.m87-star.source: VLBA · Helical structure of the M87 jet
catalog.featured-objects.ngc-604.descrip: A region where hot, massive stars form. The model shows the large gas cavities and their surrounding filaments seen in observations.
catalog.featured-objects.orion-nebula.de: A nearby star-forming region. The model shows glowing gas and the four main Trapezium stars at its center.
catalog.featured-objects.orion-nebula.so: NASA Hubble · Orion Nebula and Trapezium
catalog.featured-objects.pillars-of-crea: A star-forming region in the Eagle Nebula. The gas and dust pillars are modeled after Hubble and Webb observations.
The radius follows a 2024 analysis of NICER and XMM-Newton observations. The beam model slows the fast rotation so it is visible.
catalog.featured-objects.rigel-a.descrip: The bright star at Orion's foot. Its radius is based on stellar interferometry and the Hipparcos distance estimate. The surface texture is procedural.
catalog.featured-objects.rigel-a.name: Rigel A
catalog.featured-objects.rx-j1856.descri: A nearby isolated neutron star with a distance estimated from Hubble parallax. XMM-Newton detected weak X-ray pulsations every 7.055 seconds. The rotating bright spot illustrates the pulsation.
catalog.featured-objects.sgr-1806.catalo: McGill Magnetar Catalog · Position and spin
catalog.featured-objects.sgr-1806.descri: A magnetar whose giant flare was observed on December 27, 2004. The map distance is an estimate from spectroscopy of its associated cluster. The surface patterns, bright magnetic poles, and light moving along field lines illustrate the magnetic field.
catalog.featured-objects.sn-1987a.descri: A supernova observed in 1987. The model shows central ejecta, the equatorial ring lit by shocks, and the fainter outer rings.
catalog.featured-objects.uy-scuti.descri: A red supergiant with semiregular brightness changes. The radius and distance come from a VLTI study that assumed about 9,500 light-years. The brightness animation uses a representative period. The surface texture is procedural.
catalog.featured-objects.uy-scuti.name: UY Scuti
catalog.kepler-16.doyle.source.doyle-et-: Doyle et al. · Binary and planetary orbits
catalog.kepler-16.kepler-16-b.note: A gas planet orbiting the binary's common barycenter. Its orbital plane and initial phase are simplified, and its atmosphere is illustrative.
catalog.kepler-16.kepler-16-secondary.no: A low-mass red dwarf. Its effective temperature and luminosity are estimates from a stellar model.
catalog.kepler-16.kepler-16.summary: A binary about 245 light-years away. The stars orbit their barycenter in about 41.08 days, and Kepler-16 b in about 228.8 days.
catalog.local-group.local-group.name: Local Group
catalog.local-group.local-group.summary: Nearby galaxies are plotted at their observed directions and distances on a common scale relative to the Milky Way.
catalog.m31-eclipsing-binary.m31v-j00443: An eclipsing binary in Andromeda. The stars orbit their barycenter in about 2.049 days. From the default Earth-facing view, play at one day per second to see the eclipses. The initial orbital phase is illustrative.
catalog.m31-eclipsing-binary.note: Luminosity is estimated from the published radius and effective temperature. The surface is modeled as a sphere.
catalog.m31-eclipsing-binary.source.sour: Vilardell et al. · Eclipsing binary observations and modeling
catalog.m87.m87.name: Messier 87
catalog.m87.m87.summary: A giant elliptical galaxy in the Virgo Cluster, about 54 million light-years away. The model shows a smooth stellar distribution.
catalog.m87.m87.title: Messier 87 · M87
catalog.magellanic-clouds.large-magellan: A dwarf satellite of the Milky Way about 160,000 light-years away. The model shows its bright bar and asymmetric stellar distribution.
catalog.magellanic-clouds.small-magellan: A dwarf satellite of the Milky Way about 206,000 light-years away. The model shows its elongated, irregular stellar distribution.
catalog.milky-way.milky-way.name: Milky Way
catalog.milky-way.milky-way.diskNote: The disk texture is NASA’s reconstructed external view based on Spitzer observations. The model points follow the brightness and colors of the reconstruction.
catalog.milky-way.milky-way.notes: Dashed lines show circular orbit models through the current locations. Actual galactic orbits vary between systems.
catalog.milky-way.milky-way.summary: A model of the barred spiral galaxy, with two major spiral arms extending from the ends of its central bar.

catalog.nearby-exoplanets.gliese12.summa: A red dwarf about 40 light-years away. Its confirmed planet Gliese 12 b is similar in size to Earth and orbits in about 12.76 days.
catalog.nearby-exoplanets.lhs1140.summar: A red dwarf about 49 light-years away. Compare the orbits of its confirmed transiting planets b and c.
catalog.nearby-exoplanets.transit-model: Orbital period, semimajor axis, and radius use published estimates. The circular orbit, initial phase, and surface are illustrative.
catalog.nearby-groups.fornax.name: Fornax Cluster
catalog.nearby-groups.fornax.summary: A nearby galaxy cluster roughly 60 million light-years away. The map shows two representative members, NGC 1399 and NGC 1365.
catalog.nearby-groups.hydra-i.name: Hydra I Galaxy Cluster
catalog.nearby-groups.hydra-i.summary: Also known as Abell 1060. The map shows the central galaxies NGC 3311 and NGC 3309 at the same adopted cluster distance.
catalog.nearby-groups.leo-i.name: Leo I Galaxy Group
catalog.nearby-groups.leo-i.summary: Also known as the M96 Group. This map shows M95, M96, and M105 at adopted distances of about 32–35 million light-years.
catalog.nearby-groups.m105.summary: An elliptical galaxy in the Leo I Group. The map uses the Hubble Messier catalog estimate of about 32 million light-years.
catalog.nearby-groups.m81-group.name: M81 Galaxy Group
catalog.nearby-groups.m81-group.summary: This galaxy group lies about 12 million light-years away in Ursa Major. This map shows M81, M82, and NGC 3077.
catalog.nearby-groups.m81.summary: A spiral galaxy at an estimated distance of 11.6 million light-years in the Hubble catalog.
catalog.nearby-groups.m82.summary: A starburst galaxy interacting with M81. Its nearly edge-on disk gives it a cigar-like appearance.
catalog.nearby-groups.m95.summary: A barred spiral galaxy. The map uses the Hubble catalog distance estimate of about 33 million light-years.
catalog.nearby-groups.m96.summary: A spiral galaxy in the Leo I Group. The map uses a rounded Hubble catalog distance estimate of about 35 million light-years.
catalog.nearby-groups.ngc1365.summary: A barred spiral galaxy in Fornax. The map uses the Webb image catalog’s estimate of about 56 million light-years.
catalog.nearby-groups.ngc1399.summary: A giant elliptical galaxy near the center of Fornax. The map uses the approximate cluster distance of 60 million light-years.
catalog.nearby-groups.ngc3077.summary: A small galaxy near M81 and M82. The map adopts the published distance estimate of approximately 3.83 Mpc.
catalog.nearby-groups.ngc3309.summary: A giant elliptical seen close to NGC 3311. Both are plotted at the adopted cluster distance.
catalog.nearby-groups.ngc3311.summary: A giant elliptical near the center of Hydra I. The map adopts the cluster’s estimated distance of about 154 million light-years.
catalog.nearby-showcase.centaurus-a.name: Centaurus A
catalog.nearby-showcase.centaurus-a.summ: A galaxy with a prominent dark dust lane crossing its center. The map adopts the Webb estimate of about 11 million light-years.
catalog.nearby-showcase.m51-pair.name: Whirlpool Galaxy Pair
catalog.nearby-showcase.m51-pair.summary: Explore M51 and its companion NGC 5195 together. This map uses a common distance for the pair.
catalog.nearby-showcase.m51.name: Whirlpool Galaxy
catalog.nearby-showcase.m51.summary: A spiral galaxy interacting with NGC 5195. The map adopts the Hubble catalog estimate of about 31 million light-years.
catalog.nearby-showcase.ngc253.name: Sculptor Galaxy
catalog.nearby-showcase.ngc253.summary: A nearby spiral galaxy with active star formation. The map uses the ESO distance estimate of about 11 million light-years.
catalog.nearby-showcase.ngc5195.summary: The interacting companion of the Whirlpool Galaxy. The map uses a common distance for both galaxies to show their angular separation.
catalog.observable-universe.3c-273.summa: Hubble imaged a bright core and a one-sided jet. Hubble data guide the distribution of the bright knots in the model. Relativistic Doppler boosting can brighten an approaching jet and make its receding counterpart difficult to detect.
catalog.observable-universe.j0313-1806.s: Wang et al. · J0313−1806 discovery and ALMA observations
This quasar already hosted a supermassive black hole about 670 million years after the Big Bang. ALMA measured its redshift from a carbon emission line in the host galaxy.
catalog.observable-universe.jades-gs-z14: Carniani et al. · Discovery paper and coordinates
Schouws et al. · ALMA redshift measurement
A compact, bright galaxy seen about 300 million years after the Big Bang. Webb confirmed it, and ALMA later refined its redshift using oxygen emission.
catalog.observable-universe.observable-u: NASA · Size of the observable universe
catalog.observable-universe.ton-618.summ: TON 618 is the bright active nucleus of a distant galaxy. Infalling material heats the accretion disk around its supermassive black hole.

catalog.planets.neptune.name: Neptune
catalog.planets.neptune.surface: The reconstructed cloud map shows the Great Dark Spot and nearby bright clouds as seen by Voyager 2 in 1989. Later Hubble observations showed that this storm had vanished.
catalog.planets.saturn.atmosphere: Cassini observations informed the model of the hexagonal jet stream around the north pole. The rings use an observation-based texture for their bands and gaps.

details.blackHoleLensing: The arcs around the shadow illustrate how gravitational lensing bends light from background stars.
details.blackHoleFlow: The inner plasma orbits faster than the outer flow. The animation and playback speed illustrate this motion.
details.blackHoleFlares: Webb’s infrared flicker and flare observations inspired the added highlights. The color and shape of the blue arcs are based on NASA’s artist’s concept.
details.clusterModelScale: The scale bar measures distance within the cluster model. Star positions and brightnesses are illustrative samples.
details.commonScaleEnlarged: Orbital distances share a scale. Bodies are enlarged for visibility.
details.cosmicMapSymbols: The rendered sizes and textures help distinguish objects on the map.
details.cosmicModelScale: The universe map uses comoving distance. The detail model is shown out of scale.
details.webbRingGalaxyModel: The rings and spokes incorporate color and brightness from Webb’s near- and mid-infrared composite. The disk thickness is illustrative.
details.ehtIntensityImage: The model’s bright ring incorporates the brightness pattern from the Event Horizon Telescope’s 2022 reconstruction of its 2017 radio observations.
details.ehtPolarizationImage: The model’s ring incorporates the Event Horizon Telescope’s 2024 polarized image. Lines in the original image show the observed polarization orientation.
details.expansionModel: Expansion model · Approximate changes in {0} over up to 25 years.
details.fixedJ2000: Simulation using fixed J2000 orbital elements
details.galaxyModel: The galaxy's shape and colors are illustrative.
details.galaxyObservationDisk: The stellar points and light inside the disk follow the brightness and color of the observation image. Its thickness and depth are illustrative.
details.galaxyModelScale: The map uses the galaxy’s direction and distance. Its stellar distribution and structure are illustrative.
details.irradianceAtSemimajorAxis: Stellar irradiance at the orbital semimajor axis
details.logRadiusScale: Logarithmic scale · Radius increases tenfold per interval
details.modeledOrbits: The orbits of {0} show modeled changes in distance over one revolution.
details.nebulaObservationVolume: A James Webb Space Telescope infrared image supplies the color and detail for this 3D gas model. Depth and the far side are illustrative.
details.hubbleObservationVolume: Hubble imagery supplies the color and detail for this 3D model. Depth and the far side are illustrative.
details.nebulaModelScale: The scale bar measures distance within the model. The nebula’s boundaries and internal structure are reconstructions based on observations.
details.oortCloudModel: The sphere shows the estimated extent. Blue dots are simulated samples, and the orange dot is the Sun.
details.proceduralSurfaces: Surfaces are procedural. Bodies and moon distances are enlarged.
details.pulsarRadius: Radius about {0} km · Roughly 1/{1} of the Sun's radius (model value)
details.superclusterBoundaries: The rings mark distance. The structure's boundaries depend on observations and classification criteria.
details.systemDistance: Solar System to this star system
details.systemModelScale: Body surfaces are visual models. Body sizes and some moon orbits are enlarged, so they differ from the values above when measured with the scene scale.
details.universeLayout: Objects are placed by observed direction and comoving distance. The rings mark distance.
details.universeRadius: The observable universe extends roughly 46 billion light-years from our vantage point near Earth.
details.unscaledModel: The on-screen model does not represent the object’s physical radius or angular diameter.
details.virgoClusterMembers: Select a galaxy label or a name below to open its model.
details.virgoClusterScale: Galaxies are placed using their observed directions and estimated distances. The rings are distance guides for this map.
